summary: Okanogan NF site: a 1934 firefinder camp, a 1935 L-4 cab, and the cab removed or destroyed in 1952. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Camp with firefinders, two stations about a quarter mile apart (1934), then an L-4 cab (1935)
facts.status_note: Sources differ on how the L-4 cab ended: FFLOS says it was removed in 1952, Willhite reports it was said to be removed that year, and Firelookout.com says it was destroyed. No source describes what remains.

events.note: Camp with firefinders, with stations about a quarter mile apart
Panoramic photographs taken at both stations on September 20, 1934
L-4 cab placed at the site, replacing the firefinder camp
L-4 cab removed in 1952 per FFLOS; Willhite reports it was said to be removed; Firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered as US 1432, WA 332 on November 9, 2012

evidence.supports: 1934 camp with firefinders; L-4 cab in 1935 replaced it; cab removed in 1952
evidence.quote: In 1934, a camp with firefinders was built 1/4 mile north and south. This was replaced in 1935 with an L-4 cab, which was removed in 1952.

evidence.supports: Camp with firefinders in 1934; L-4 cab in 1935; destroyed in 1952

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the L-4 cab was removed in 1952, and Willhite reports it was said to be removed that year. Firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year. The story reports both; the sources do not say how the cab was taken down.

notes_for_editor: The brief's county, status and elevation (2301.8 m matches 7,552 ft on Firelookout.com) hold up. No staffing, fire, access or present-day description found, so those keys are omitted. The removed-versus-destroyed question is unresolved.
